title: Configuring Sensitive Information: Indexed Documents Match (IDM) Settings

blocks.text: On the Indexed Document Match Settings page, (Data Security > Endpoint DLP > Endpoint Data Scan > Sensitive Information > Indexed Document Match), you can configure an Indexed Document Match (IDM) template and assign it to users who handle sensitive data and are allowed to index these documents.
To configure a template and assign it to a user, do the following:

blocks.item: 1. Add an IDM template.
On the Templates tab, click Add Template.
The Add IDM Template drawer appears.
See image.
Enter the following details:
Template Name: The name of the template.
Description: A brief description of the template.

DLP Engine Mapping: Choose the match accuracy for the IDM templates you selected. This is the level of accuracy (i.e., the percentage of similarity) that a user-uploaded document must meet to count as a match for an indexed document.
Low Accuracy: Zscaler detects a low-accuracy match when one of the following occurs:
A user-uploaded document matches at least 25% of an indexed document.
An indexed document matches at least 50% of a user-uploaded document.
Medium Accuracy: Zscaler detects a medium-accuracy match when one of the following occurs:
A user-uploaded document matches at least 50% of an indexed document.
An indexed document matches at least 75% of a user-uploaded document.
High Accuracy: Zscaler detects a high-accuracy match when a user-uploaded document matches at least 75% of an indexed document.
When processing a file, the endpoint determines its match accuracy based on priority, starting with High, then Medium, and then Low. The process halts once a valid match is confirmed.
Select Exclude 100% Match if you do not want Zscaler to trigger the dictionary for documents that are a 100% match of already indexed documents.
Click Add.
The IDM template is listed in the table.
2. Assign a template to a user.
On the Users tab, click Add User.
The Add User drawer appears. You can assign one or more templates to a user.
See image.
Select the User.
In the Assign Templates field, select the configured templates from the drop-down menu.
Click Add.
The user is assigned the template that you selected.

blocks.text: To enable the changes, you must activate the change. You can edit or delete any template or user that you added.
The IDM process is broken down as follows:

blocks.item: Configure and Authorize: Admins create IDM templates that define the detection logic and map it to the DLP engine based on match accuracy. Then they define which users are authorized to index sensitive documents from their endpoints. They can assign specific, multiple, or any template to those authorized users.
Configure DLP Rules: Admins configure Endpoint DLP rules using the IDM-linked DLP engines to enforce policies.
Index Files: Authorized users can right-click sensitive files on their endpoint and select the Index Documents option. This creates and uploads file fingerprints to the cloud.
See image.

Users can select up to 20 files per operation. The maximum size is 100 MB per file, and the total maximum file size per session cannot exceed 1 GB. Users can choose one or more IDM templates to associate with the selected files.
Activate Policy: New fingerprints appear in the admin portal for review. The admin activates the policy, distributing the updated IDM package to all endpoints.
Enforce Endpoint DLP Rule: Endpoint DLP enforces rules, detecting and acting upon full or partial matches of indexed content based on predefined accuracy thresholds.
Log Incidents: All detected incidents are logged for reporting and investigation. To learn more, see About User Investigation.
